title: Nonprofit or community organiser
summary: A mission-led community profile: explain who you serve, pair participation with transparent evidence, and list useful activities.

notFor: Companies with a social mission selling products (start from small-business)

cards.purpose: Explain the mission, who is served and how to participate.
Donate or volunteer through the group’s own destinations.
Qualified, dated financial information and a link to the full report.
Three or four recurring or confirmed community activities.
Contact, transparency and public community channels.

slots.ask: What name do you want at the top of the page?
slots.write: Exactly as they give it. Never shorten or translate it.

slots.ask: In one line, what do you do and for whom?
slots.write: One sentence, at most 120 characters, no hashtags or emoji. This appears in the About popover, not beside the name; repeat the essential purpose in the first text card.

slots.ask: What does your organisation do, for whom, and where? Are you registered?
slots.write: Plain words, two short paragraphs. Registration number exactly as on the official register. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: What should people know before taking this action: who it is for, format, timing, price or reply expectations, only if you want to publish them?
slots.write: One or two short sentences, at most 400 characters. Include only facts supplied for this action; do not assume an introductory call is free or that any date, price or reply time is current. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: What do you most need from visitors: donations, volunteers, both? Share the links.
slots.write: Heading = the impact in one concrete line they can stand behind; text = what a typical gift does, only as they state it. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: What short heading should introduce this action?
slots.write: Use a clear heading that describes the action; no unconfirmed availability or promise. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: Do you publish how donations are spent?
slots.write: Figures only from their published accounts, with a link to them. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: What regular sessions or upcoming events should people know about?
slots.write: tag = schedule or date; title = event; description = public venue and who it is for. Select up to four featured entries for this page; link to the complete archive or catalogue instead of deleting the person’s remaining work. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: How should people contact you, and which accounts should be linked?
slots.write: Prefer a contact page over a personal email. Account URLs only. Use only their confirmed information; replace or remove every demonstration name, claim, number, price, quote, date and URL in this field. Never keep sample copy as a fallback.

slots.ask: Do you want a place on your profile? A city or region is enough.
slots.write: As they write it. Never infer it.

slots.ask: Do you have a website of your own?
Do you have a photo, artwork or logo you want to upload as the profile picture?
slots.write: The person uploads their chosen picture in the editor. Never fetch, generate or infer a personal photo. Use their description for alt text wherever the editor asks for it.
